evidence.claim: Division J is micro-averaged over all videos of a split (TP/FP/FN summed). So adding one fork of evaluable precision p raises J iff p > TP/(TP+D) = J/(1+J). The break-even algebra in the hypothesis is correct.
evidence.source: tools/official/src/tracking_cellmot/metrics.py evaluate_datasets (read in the previous session, see notes); royerlab/kaggle-cell-tracking-competition README ('micro-averaged Jaccard') https://github.com/royerlab/kaggle-cell-tracking-competition

evidence.claim: The same threshold follows from the F1 result: the F1-optimal threshold on calibrated scores is F1*/2. Because F1 = 2J/(1+J), this equals J/(1+J).
evidence.source: Lipton, Elkan, Narayanaswamy 2014, 'Thresholding Classifiers to Maximize F1', arXiv:1402.1892 https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.1892

evidence.claim: The raise has no support at the margin. On SELECTION (64 6bba videos) cap 4 -> 6 at t0.6 added 50 insertions (195 -> 245) for 0 TP and +2 FP evaluable, and the score fell by 0.00034 (s_c4_t0.6 12/23/52 = +0.00499 vs s_c6_t0.6 12/25/52 = +0.00465 over exp39). Cap 2 -> 4 was still positive: +84 insertions, +2 TP / +4 FP, marginal p = 0.33.

The cap-4 insertion transfers weakly. On CONFIRMATION (135 videos) s_c4_t0.5 went from 16/28/71 to 20/39/67 (+0.00194, 90% CI [-0.0007, +0.0050]): 44b6 +1 TP / +3 FP on 4 changed videos, 6bba +3 TP / +8 FP on 8 changed videos. That is 466 insertions for 15 evaluable, about 3%. The public LB gain was +0.001 (probe 28), so local division deltas transfer at <= ~50%.

The 'public J reflects few GT divisions' argument is weak. A binomial/Poisson simulation at our train recall (23/151) and FP rate (43 per 151 GT) gives P(J >= 0.32) = 0.11 with 5 GT divisions, 0.029 with 10, 0.004 with 20 and ~0 with 45. Train GT rates are 0.37 divisions per video (44b6) and 0.98 per video (6bba), so a ~40-60 video public embryo likely holds 15-50 GT divisions. Other teams also infer high public division J (~0.22-0.28), so the public embryo looks systematically division-easier, not just noisy. The private embryo is unknown: use a mixture prior (J 0.13..0.36, mean ~0.245, break-even ~0.20) rather than 0.12.
evidence.source: own simulation (notes file); research/discussions_summary.md. The 15-50 count is an estimate.

evidence.claim: The public 0.947 -> 0.911 drop with zero forks also includes the edge-J loss from dropping each fork's second edge, so 0.36 is an upper estimate of public division J.
evidence.source: research/discussions_summary.md (remark that the zero-fork drop mixes the division term and division edges)

evidence.claim: The data refute density scaling of the cap. Per-video GT divisions vs predicted node count: Spearman 0.02 over 199 videos. 44b6 is flat by node tercile (0.38/0.39/0.33 per video) and 6bba rises modestly (0.58/0.98/1.37). GT divisions follow ANNOTATION coverage (rho 0.30 with edge TP), not nuclear density. A track-scaled cap would mostly add forks in dense, unannotated regions, where they are free but useless.
evidence.source: own analysis on the 199-video lab cache (notes file)

evidence.claim: Only ~3% of insertions are evaluable, so cap 4 -> 8 on 199 videos adds roughly 10-15 evaluable forks. The binomial 90% CI on p with n ~12 is about +-0.2, so no lab run can tell marginal p = 0.17 from 0.30. The proposed 'marginal p >= 0.17 on BOTH embryos' criterion is unreachable for 44b6 (1 TP / 3 FP evaluable in total at cap 4 on confirmation).
evidence.source: arithmetic on the confirmation counts above

evidence.claim: A Kaggle dataset states that the 4 VISIBLE test volumes are train twins (44b6_0113de3b, 44b6_0b24845f, 6bba_05b6850b, 6bba_05db0fb1). This concerns the visible sample, not the hidden scored set. It does not change this analysis, but exclude those 4 IDs from any precision estimate meant to mimic unseen data.

implementation_notes:
Code knobs (tools/div_insert.py): steal, cap_video (default 3), cap_frame (1), alpha (1.0), threshold (0.5), steal_prob_max 0.3, steal_margin 0.2, steal_frac 0.5 (steals <= floor(0.5*cap_video)). Eligible triples are ranked by score = p_par(u) * p_dau(v) * p_dau(c1)^alpha and inserted greedily, with each node used once, per-frame cap 1 and the per-video cap. The stats counters divins_skipped_cap_video, divins_skipped_cap_frame and divins_added_steal show which cap binds.

Pitfalls:
(1) Above cap 4, cap_frame = 1 and the used-node exclusion start to bind, so raising cap_video alone may add fewer insertions than expected; log divins_skipped_cap_frame.
(2) Each insertion also changes the EDGE term: the second daughter edge is FP when c1 is annotated with a different GT predecessor, and a steal removes an existing edge. On selection the adjusted edge term moved only +0.00006, but check it per cap.
(3) Local p is optimistic: DaughterNet p is OOF, but the candidate pool and graph come from a detector and edge net trained on all 199 videos.
(4) Marginal evaluable counts per cap step are tiny (0 TP / 2 FP for cap 4 -> 6 on selection), so choosing a cap from them is noise-fitting.
(5) Scenario reweighting needs a scenario-specific D: for J_s, dJ ~ (dTP*(1+J_s) - J_s*(dTP+dFP)) / D_s. Report dTP/dFP and the sign under J_s in {0.13, 0.20, 0.25, 0.36}, not a single number.
(6) Do not scale the cap by track count; the data show no link between density and GT divisions.
refined_change: Do NOT raise the per-video cap and do NOT add a track-scaled cap. Keep the shipped DaughterNet config (cap 4, steals on): the measured marginal beyond cap 4 is 0 TP / 2 FP, and density scaling is refuted. If the second, private-leaning final needs a division variant, use the one knob with positive marginal evidence: a looser score threshold at cap 4. Going from t 0.6 to 0.5 added +1 TP / +2 FP on selection (p = 0.33), which is above break-even under every J scenario up to 0.36; first check that 0.5 is not already the shipped value (probe 28 config). For a J-invariant gain, pair the unchanged insertion with fork REMOVAL, which helps under any J (e.g. the AUDIT7 fork-midpoint >= 4 um rule, 11 FP / 0 TP; see fork-midpoint-filter).
expected_gain: ~0. Private gain likely in [-0.0003, +0.0005] and sign-uncertain: the measured marginal p beyond cap 4 is 0/2 and the private division J is unknown (mixture break-even ~0.20). The claimed +0.001..+0.002 needs marginal p ~0.25 at J ~0.13 and is not supported by the data. Public: 0 to -0.0005. The division budget is better spent on J-invariant fork removal.
